headline: Google's agent toolkit Antigravity SDK can now run its coding agents on local models, so code does not have to leave the developer's computer.
score_reason: Developer feature with a privacy angle; results come from one Google demo.
importance_line: It matters to developers and firms that cannot send code to the cloud and want lower cloud costs, though the figures come from one Google demonstration and the setup needs a powerful computer.
summary: InfoQ reports, citing Google, that the Antigravity SDK, Google's toolkit for building AI coding agents, now supports local models, so a cloud model can plan a job while agents on the developer's own machine do the code work. In a Google demonstration fixing three vulnerable Python modules, Google says only 95 of about 3,400 tokens were used in the cloud and no source code was uploaded; the recommended hardware is 24GB or more of graphics or unified memory.
notes: Announcement date not stated by InfoQ; figures are Google's.
